notes:
Need to search first.I wasn't able to research Proverbs 28 this time, so I have no notes for you yet.

My first attempt to open the commentary pages (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub) failed. The tool only opens pages that have already turned up in a search, and I hadn't searched first. When I then ran the searches, I'd hit the limit on tool calls for this turn, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Since I didn't read any pages, I haven't written any notes. Writing them from memory would break those rules.

If you send the request again, I'll search first and then read the pages, in this order:
1. **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and the Bible Hub and StudyLight commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** the most likely verses are v. 9 (whether God hears prayer from someone who ignores the law), v. 13 (confessing sin and finding mercy), and v. 14 (always fearing God versus hardening the heart). I'll check Wesley's notes, Spurgeon, Ligonier/The Gospel Coalition and the LCMS/1517 sites for these.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and the Catholic sites (catholic.com, newadvent.org). For prosperity teaching, vv. 19–20, 25 and 27 are the likely places, and I'll only include it if the sites actually discuss those verses.

It may take a few turns to cover all 28 verses well. I could do it in batches (vv. 1–10, 11–20, 21–28) if that suits you.
